paragraphs: A recorder of Hanseo—the boy who knows what he loves and pursues it with fire—as he grows into a young man.
In his room hangs a note: “Make today happier than yesterday.” He seems, to me, to know how to live in the present.

Looking at him, I sometimes feel the weight of my own past regrets—places I never went, languages I never learned. In the heat he carries, that regret turns into a resolve to focus more fully on now. Even now.

He is one of the dear friends who make me feel all of this. In 2026 he has taken up the camera. He has become a colleague. In his photographs I see the present being held. And I cheer him on—him, and myself.
